newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SUSPENSION OF SLOVAK REFERENDUM ILLEGAL - OPPOSITION.
newsitem.headline: SUSPENSION OF SLOVAK REFERENDUM ILLEGAL - OPPOSITION.

text.p: Slovak opposition leaders said on Wednesday a government order to suspend preparations for a referendum on direct presidential elections was illegal.

On Tuesday, deputy premier Katarina Tothova said the cabinet had asked the Constitutional Court to rule on whether the constitution could be changed by a referendum and told the authorities responsible for organising the plebiscite to suspend preparations until the court ruling.

"The referendum must take place regardless of the ruling of the Constitutional Court," Social Democrat leader Jaroslav Volf told independent radio Twist. "The government's attitude can be described as contempt for the law."
President Michal Kovac last month set two referendums on May 23 and 24 on direct presidential elections and on whether Slovakia should join NATO.
The NATO referendum was called by Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar's Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS), while the other resulted from a petition initiated by the opposition.

"If the government is able to act in this undemocratic way, the opposition must prepare certain counter-measures," Bela Bugar, chairman of the ethnic Hungarian Christian-Democratic Movement told a news conferenece on Wednesday.
The opposition called for the presidential referendum in an attempt to prevent Meciar assuming presidential powers when Kovac's term of office expires next March.

In its present composition the Slovak parliament would be unable to muster the necessary two-thirds majority to elect a new president, which would mean presidential powers would be delegated to the government, effectively to Meciar.
Kovac, who supported the direct presidential election, announced on Wednesday he would hold a news conference on the issue on Thursday.
